mainTopic: When an אשם תלוי is brought: the משנה's doubt cases, and whether a single doubtful piece is enough or two pieces are needed
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה about the אשם תלוי, the offering brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned. The משנה gives three classic doubt cases: two pieces of fat, his wife and his sister, and שבת and a weekday. It then rules that אשם תלוי offerings are counted just like חטאת offerings. In the גמרא, רב אסי and חייא בר רב argue whether the משנה means a single doubtful piece or one piece out of two. Their argument depends on whether we follow the spelling of the word מצות (singular) or its reading מצוות (plural). רב rules that one of two pieces obligates an אשם תלוי, while a single doubtful piece exempts. רבא explains this from the plural reading. Sources that require an אשם תלוי for a single doubt, such as the כוי, the יבם's doubtful child and the blood found on the cloth, are answered as following רבי אליעזר. רבי זירא gives a different reason: the doubt must be one that can be checked. The two reasons differ in a case of an olive-size piece and a half-olive piece.

steps.title: Finishing the previous rule: even without a full measure
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the previous line of the משנה: the ruling holds even if there was not a full measure in the piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Whether there is a full measure or whether] there is not in it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is just the tail end of a sentence that started before this section. The משנה is finishing its rule that he brings an אשם תלוי whether or not the piece had the size that makes one liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous line taught that someone unsure whether he ate forbidden fat brings an אשם תלוי. These two words complete the thought that this is true even when the piece lacked the full measure. It closes off that rule before the משנה moves on to new cases.

keyTerms.meaning: There is not in it, meaning the piece did not have the full measure

phrases.english: there is not in it
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before: whether the piece had the full measure or did not have it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a rule from the previous part of the משנה, which is outside this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The previous ruling applies even when the piece did not have the full measure.

steps.title: Three doubt cases that require an uncertain guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three cases where a person did one of two acts, one permitted and one forbidden, and does not know which one he did. In all of them he brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If permitted fat and forbidden fat were in front of him, he ate one, and he does not know which one; or if his wife and his sister were in the house with him, he was with one of them by mistake, and he does not know which one; or if there was שבת and a weekday, he did מלאכה on one of them, and he does not know which day it was, then he brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives three examples of a real doubt: he definitely did one of two things, but he does not know whether it was the forbidden one. Each time the answer is the same: he brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has the same pattern: one permitted option and one forbidden option, and he did exactly one of them. Since he may have done a sin that would require a חטאת if he did it knowingly, he brings an אשם תלוי to protect himself while the doubt remains. The three cases cover eating (חלב), forbidden relations (his sister), and שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted animal fat
Forbidden fat, which carries כרת if eaten on purpose and requires a חטאת if eaten by mistake
A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he did a sin that would require a חטאת
He sinned by mistake, without intending to
Work that is forbidden on שבת
An ordinary weekday

steps.whatToRemember: An אשם תלוי needs a real doubt between two things, one permitted and one forbidden, and he certainly did one of them.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up שומן and חלב. Both mean fat, but שומן here is the permitted kind and חלב is the forbidden kind.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three cases are the standard examples of 'one of two pieces', the classic setup for an אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: permitted fat and forbidden fat are before him
and he ate one of them
and he does not know which of them he ate
his wife and his sister were with him in the house
he unwittingly sinned with one of them
and he does not know with which of them he sinned
Shabbat and a weekday
and he did labor on one of them
and he does not know on which of them he did it
he brings a provisional guilt offering

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the previous rule to a new set of 'one of two' doubt cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a doubt where he did one of two acts, one permitted and one forbidden, he brings an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: One lapse of awareness means only one uncertain guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: Just as eating forbidden fat twice in one lapse of awareness requires only one חטאת, eating two doubtful pieces in one lapse requires only one אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as when someone ate forbidden fat and more forbidden fat in one lapse of awareness he owes only one חטאת, so in their uncertain cases he brings only one אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now asks how many offerings are needed when the doubt happened more than once. It answers by comparing to the rule of חטאת: one lapse of awareness means one offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a חטאת, all the sins done during a single stretch of not knowing count as one, so he brings one חטאת. The משנה applies the same counting rule to the אשם תלוי. Several doubtful eatings in one lapse need only one אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: One lapse of awareness: a single stretch of time in which he did not realize he was sinning
A sin offering, brought for a definite sin done by mistake
'It was not made known', meaning the uncertain cases where he never found out for sure

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a rule that the אשם תלוי follows the same counting system as the חטאת.

phrases.english: just as if one ate forbidden fat and forbidden fat
in a single lapse of awareness
phrases.notes: Some versions say אחת and some say אחד; either way it means one lapse.

phrases.english: he is liable to only one sin offering
so too, for their unknown cases
phrases.notes: This means the doubtful cases, where he never found out whether he actually sinned.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אֶלָּא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי אֶחָד.
phrases.english: he brings only one provisional guilt offering

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִם אָכַל חֵלֶב וָחֵלֶב בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the doubt cases and asks how many offerings are owed when it happened more than once.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Several doubtful sins in one lapse of awareness require only one אשם תלוי, just like one חטאת for several definite sins.

steps.title: Awareness in between means an offering for each
steps.stepSummary: If he became aware in between the acts, then just as he would bring a separate חטאת for each, he brings a separate אשם תלוי for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there was awareness in between, then just as he brings a חטאת for each one, so too he brings an אשם תלוי for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of the rule. If the lapse was broken by a moment of awareness, each act counts on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Becoming aware between the acts splits them into separate lapses. For a חטאת, that means one offering per act, and the אשם תלוי follows the same pattern. This completes the comparison between the two offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness in between: he realized something between the first act and the second
For each and every one, separately

steps.whatToRemember: The אשם תלוי is counted the same way as the חטאת. One lapse means one offering, and awareness in between means one offering for each act.

phrases.english: if there was awareness in between
just as he brings a sin offering
for each and every one
so he brings a provisional guilt offering
for each and every one

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 3, where the single lapse was broken by awareness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Awareness between the acts makes each one require its own אשם תלוי, just as each would require its own חטאת.

steps.title: Different kinds of forbidden food mean a separate אשם תלוי for each
steps.stepSummary: The משנה concludes: just as eating חלב, דם, פיגול and נותר in one העלם requires a separate חטאת for each, doubtful cases of these require a separate אשם תלוי for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as someone who ate forbidden fat, blood, פיגול and נותר in one lapse of awareness owes a sin offering for each one, so too, when their status was unknown to him, he brings an אשם תלוי for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its comparison between חטאת and אשם תלוי. Different kinds of forbidden food each need their own אשם תלוי, even within one העלם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 taught that two pieces of the same forbidden kind, eaten in one העלם, need only one offering. Here the משנה adds that different kinds (חלב, דם, פיגול, נותר) are separate sins. So each kind gets its own חטאת, and when it was only a doubt, its own אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: One lapse of awareness: the person never realized in between that he was sinning
Sacrificial meat made forbidden by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten
Sacrificial meat left over past the time it was allowed to be eaten
"Was not made known": a case where he does not know whether what he ate was forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: Same kind of sin in one העלם means one offering. Different kinds of sin mean a separate offering for each, whether it is a חטאת for a known sin or an אשם תלוי for a doubtful one.

phrases.english: Just as one who ate forbidden fat and blood
and piggul and notar in one lapse of awareness
is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every one,
so too, for their case of "not known"
phrases.notes: This means cases where he isn't sure whether what he ate was really forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת
phrases.english: he brings a provisional guilt offering for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָכַל חֵלֶב וָדָם וּפִיגּוּל וְנוֹתָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's series of parallels between חטאת and אשם תלוי by adding the case of different kinds of forbidden food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different kinds of forbidden food eaten in doubt during one העלם require a separate אשם תלוי for each kind.

steps.title: Dispute: one doubtful piece or one piece out of two
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says the משנה's case is a single piece that might be חלב or might be שומן. חייא בר רב says it is one piece out of two pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב אסי says we learned the case of one piece, which might be forbidden fat or might be permitted fat. חייא בר רב says we learned the case of one piece out of two pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting two אמוראים who disagree about what kind of doubt the משנה is describing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אסי, even a single piece of unknown status is enough to require an אשם תלוי. For חייא בר רב, there must have been two pieces, one forbidden and one permitted, and he ate one without knowing which. With only a single doubtful piece, he would not bring an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece of meat or fat
Forbidden fat; eating it carries the penalty of כרת
Permitted fat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think חייא בר רב is talking about eating both pieces. He means one piece out of two, where he ate one and does not know which one it was.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
Rav Asi says:
We learned the case of one piece,

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק שֶׁל חֵלֶב סָפֵק שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן
phrases.english: which might be forbidden fat or might be permitted fat.
Ḥiyya bar Rav says:
We learned the case of a piece out of two pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב אַסִּי אָמַר: חֲתִיכָה אַחַת שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins and goes back to the משנה's basic case of a doubtful piece of fat, to define exactly what kind of doubt is meant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אסי: a single piece of doubtful status requires an אשם תלוי. חייא בר רב: only a piece out of two, one forbidden and one permitted, requires it.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רב אסי and חייא בר רב are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the dispute. This line sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge to either opinion. The גמרא simply wants to find the underlying source or principle that splits the two אמוראים.

keyTerms.meaning: "About what do they disagree?": a request for the root of a dispute

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the dispute just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What underlying principle or source explains the disagreement between רב אסי and חייא בר רב?

steps.title: Spelling versus reading of the word מצות
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי follows the written spelling מצות, which looks singular, so one piece is enough. חייא בר רב follows the reading מצוות, which is plural, so two pieces are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי holds that the written spelling is the authority, and the word is written "מצות" (singular). חייא בר רב holds that the way we read it is the authority, and we read "מצוות" (plural).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the dispute comes from one word in the פסוק about אשם תלוי. The word is spelled one way and read another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא ה:יז the word is spelled מצות without a vav, which looks like the singular מצוַת. It is read as the plural מצוות. רב אסי says the spelling teaches the הלכה (יש אם למסורת), so a single doubtful piece is enough. חייא בר רב says the reading teaches the הלכה (יש אם למקרא), so there must be two pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: The written spelling of the תורה is the authority for learning הלכה
The traditional reading of the תורה is the authority for learning הלכה
"It is written": how the word is spelled
"We read": how the word is pronounced

steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי follows the spelling, מצות (singular), so one doubtful piece is enough. חייא בר רב follows the reading, מצוות (plural), so it must be one piece out of two.
steps.confusionAlert: Singular and plural here are not about how many sins he did. They are about how many pieces were in front of him when the doubt came up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear example of the general argument between יש אם למסורת and יש אם למקרא, which shows up in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rav Asi holds:
The written tradition is authoritative;
phrases.notes: He means we learn הלכה from how the word is spelled in the ספר תורה.

phrases.english: it is written "mitzvat" (singular).
phrases.notes: ויקרא ה:יז. The word is spelled without a vav, so it looks singular.

phrases.english: And Ḥiyya bar Rav says:
The reading is authoritative;
we read "מצוות" (plural).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַסִּי סָבַר: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמָּסוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7 by tying each opinion to a different way of learning the same word in the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אסי learns from the spelling מצות (singular), so one doubtful piece requires an אשם תלוי. חייא בר רב learns from the reading מצוות (plural), so two pieces must be involved.

steps.title: Challenge to רב אסי from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא (or חייא בר רב) challenges רב אסי: the end of the משנה speaks of two pieces, so the beginning should also be about two pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא challenged רב אסי (some say it was חייא בר רב). The משנה's later clause says: 'forbidden fat and permitted fat were before him and he ate one of them.' Doesn't that show that, just as the later clause speaks of two pieces, the first clause also speaks of two pieces?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אסי's view that one doubtful piece is enough for an אשם תלוי. It points to the end of the משנה, which clearly describes two pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is that the רישא and סיפא of a משנה usually describe the same kind of case. The סיפא clearly has two pieces, so the רישא should too. That would match חייא בר רב and go against רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The later or last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Piece / pieces (of fat)
Permitted fat

phrases.english: Rav Huna raised an objection to Rav Asi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: and some say it was Chiyya bar Rav who objected to Rav Asi:
If forbidden fat and permitted fat were before him
phrases.notes: This is the later clause of our משנה, which plainly has two separate pieces.

phrases.english: and he ate one of them.
Is it not that since the later clause is about two pieces,
the first clause is also about two pieces?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אסי's position from step 6, using the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's view that the משנה's case is a single doubtful piece
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא clearly involves two pieces, so the רישא should be read the same way, which contradicts רב אסי.

steps.title: רב deflects the proof: the two clauses can differ
steps.stepSummary: רב says the proof can be turned around: רב אסי can answer that the סיפא is about two pieces while the רישא is about one piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to them: Don't build a proof on something that can be read the other way. רב אסי can answer you: the later clause is about two pieces, but the first clause is about one piece.
steps.whatsHappening: רב pushes back on the challenge. He says nothing forces the רישא and סיפא to describe the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed both clauses must match. רב shows they don't have to: the רישא could be one doubtful piece and the סיפא two pieces. That way, the משנה stays consistent with רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite; a reading that can be turned the other way
To answer back, to give an alternative explanation

phrases.english: Rav said to them:
Do not go after the opposite,
phrases.notes: He means: don't rely on a proof that can just as easily be read the other way.

phrases.english: for he can answer you:
the later clause is about two pieces,
the first clause is about one piece.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the רישא must match the סיפא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two clauses can describe different cases: one piece in the רישא, two pieces in the סיפא.

steps.title: Then why mention two pieces at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if one doubtful piece already obligates, it is obvious that two pieces would, so why does the סיפא need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, one can ask: if he is obligated with just one piece, do we really need to be told that he is obligated with two pieces?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's answer. If the רישא already obligates with one piece, the סיפא about two pieces seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two pieces with one definitely forbidden is a stronger case for an אשם תלוי than one doubtful piece. So teaching the two-piece case after the one-piece case seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it need to be said? (meaning: it is obvious)
He is obligated

phrases.english: If so, one can say:
with one piece he is obligated,
with two pieces, does it need to be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's defense from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reading that the רישא is one piece and the סיפא is two
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one piece already obligates, the two-piece case is obvious and should not need to be taught.

steps.title: The style of 'this, and no need to say that'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה teaches the harder case first and then the easier one, in the style of 'this, and it is unnecessary to say that.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה uses the style: 'This case, and there is no need to say that case.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The משנה sometimes teaches a big new case and then adds the obvious case anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching an obvious case after a surprising one is a known style. So the extra two-piece clause does not disprove רב's reading, and רב אסי's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This, and no need to say that': teaching the bigger novelty first, then the obvious case

steps.whatToRemember: In defense of רב אסי: the סיפא's two pieces do not prove that the רישא is also about two pieces. The משנה may teach one piece first and then add the obvious two-piece case.

phrases.english: This, and it is unnecessary to say that.
phrases.notes: Some versions say לְמֵימַר; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is לוֹמַר. The meaning is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two-piece clause would be pointless if one piece already obligates.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches the bigger novelty first and then adds the obvious case.

steps.title: For חייא בר רב: why two clauses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to חייא בר רב: if both clauses are about two pieces, why does the משנה teach the same thing twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to חייא בר רב, who says that since the later clause is about two pieces the first clause is too, why do I need two clauses?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא questions the other side. If both clauses describe the same two-piece case, one seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's reading gives each clause its own case. חייא בר רב's reading seems to make the משנה repeat itself, so he needs to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need two (clauses)?

phrases.english: And according to Chiyya bar Rav, who says:
since the later clause is about two pieces,
the first clause is also about two pieces,
why do I need to teach two clauses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from defending רב אסי to questioning חייא בר רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's reading that both clauses are about two pieces
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both clauses describe the same case, the משנה is repeating itself for no reason.

steps.title: The second clause explains the first
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the סיפא is not a new case; it explains how the רישא's doubt comes about, with forbidden and permitted fat in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is explaining itself: if it is doubtful whether he ate forbidden fat or not, he brings an אשם תלוי. How so? For example, when forbidden fat and permitted fat were in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for חייא בר רב. The second clause is not extra; it explains what the first clause means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא states the rule in general terms (a doubt about eating חלב). The סיפא spells out the case: two pieces, one חלב and one שומן. So there is no repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining (the earlier clause)
How so?
Provisional guilt offering brought for a doubtful sin

phrases.english: It is explaining itself:

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק אָכַל סָפֵק לֹא אָכַל חֵלֶב
phrases.english: If it is uncertain whether he ate or did not eat forbidden fat,
he brings a provisional guilt offering.
How so?
For example, where forbidden fat and permitted fat were before him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The second clause explains the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses teach the same case, so one is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא explains the רישא by giving its concrete case, so nothing is repeated.
steps.whatToRemember: Both readings of the משנה work: רב אסי uses 'this, and no need to say that'; חייא בר רב says the סיפא explains the רישא.

steps.title: רב's ruling: two pieces obligate, one doubtful piece exempts
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: if one of two pieces (one חלב, one שומן) was eaten, he is obligated in an אשם תלוי; if a single doubtful piece was eaten, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If two pieces were in front of him, one permitted fat and one forbidden fat, and he ate one and doesn't know which, he is obligated. If there was one piece, maybe forbidden fat and maybe permitted fat, and he ate it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב that sets the rule clearly. With two pieces he brings an אשם תלוי; with one doubtful piece he does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling matches חייא בר רב's reading, which requires two pieces, one of them definitely forbidden. A single piece whose status is unclear is not enough to obligate an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated (here, to bring an אשם תלוי)
Exempt
Doubt, uncertainty

steps.confusionAlert: 'Exempt' with one piece does not mean eating it is fine. It only means he does not bring an אשם תלוי for this kind of doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the sugya, which looks for the reason behind רב's distinction between one piece and two pieces.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If there were two pieces before him,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן וְאַחַת שֶׁל חֵלֶב,
phrases.english: one of permitted fat and one of forbidden fat,
and he ate one of them

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אֵיזוֹ מֵהֶן אָכַל – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and does not know which of them he ate, he is obligated.
If there was one piece,

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק שֶׁל חֵלֶב סָפֵק שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן
phrases.english: maybe of forbidden fat, maybe of permitted fat,
and he ate it, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new statement from רב that sets the rule in the one-piece versus two-piece question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two pieces, one forbidden: obligated in an אשם תלוי. One doubtful piece: exempt.

steps.title: רבא explains the source for רב's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב's rule comes from the פסוק's word מצות. It is spelled like a singular but read as a plural, so the doubt must involve two items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רב's reason? The פסוק says 'and he does one of all the commandments of ה' unknowingly.' This teaches that he is not liable until he is unsure between two things. The word is spelled 'מצות' (commandment), but we read it as 'מצוות' (commandments).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the source for רב's ruling from the step before. A single doubtful piece is exempt, but one of two pieces obligates an אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word in the פסוק could be read as singular or plural. The way we pronounce it is plural, 'commandments.' רב builds on that reading: there must be two items in front of the person, one forbidden and one permitted, before an אשם תלוי applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (asking for the source of a ruling)
Doing something wrong by mistake, without knowing
It is written (how the word is spelled in the Torah)
We read it (how the word is pronounced)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'כתיב' and 'קרינן.' כתיב is the spelling, here singular. קרינן is the reading, here plural. רב follows the reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole debate that follows. Following the reading gives רב's rule (two pieces needed). Following the spelling gives the opposite (one piece is enough).

phrases.english: Rava said: What is the reason of Rav?
For the verse says:
"And he does one of all the commandments of the Lord unknowingly"
– not until he is mistaken between two,
"Mitzvat" (singular) is written,
but we read it "מצוות" (plural).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the תורה source for רב's ruling stated in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם תלוי is brought only when the doubt is between two items. This is learned from the plural reading 'מצוות.'

steps.title: אביי objects from רבי אליעזר's ruling on a כוי
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites רבי אליעזר, who requires an אשם תלוי for the fat of a כוי. That is a single item of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: רבי אליעזר says that for a כוי, one is obligated to bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's explanation. Here is a case where one doubtful item, not two, still requires an אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוי is an animal of unclear type. Its fat is forbidden if it counts as a domestic animal and permitted if it counts as a wild one. Eating its fat involves only one piece, whose status is itself unclear. Yet רבי אליעזר requires an אשם תלוי, which seems to go against the idea that the פסוק needs two items.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with signs of both a domestic and a wild animal, so its status is in doubt
A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
Rabbi Eliezer says: a koy –
phrases.notes: The point is that you eat the fat of the כוי itself. There is just one piece, with no permitted piece beside it.

phrases.english: one is obligated to bring a provisional guilt offering for it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's explanation of רב in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that an אשם תלוי requires doubt between two items
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר obligates an אשם תלוי for a single doubtful item (the כוי's fat). This contradicts the derivation from the plural 'מצוות.'

steps.title: רבי אליעזר follows the written spelling
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבי אליעזר holds the spelling counts. The spelling is singular, so for him one item of doubt is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: רבי אליעזר holds that the written spelling is what counts, and 'מצות' (singular) is what is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's challenge. רבי אליעזר simply reads the same פסוק differently from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is about which counts more, the spelling or the pronunciation. רב follows the pronunciation (plural), so he needs two items. רבי אליעזר follows the spelling (singular), so one doubtful item is enough. רב's view is therefore not disproved; he just holds a different opinion than רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The written spelling is the main authority for learning from a פסוק
The handed-down way the words are spelled in the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: רב follows the reading: 'מצוות,' plural, so two items are needed. רבי אליעזר follows the spelling: 'מצות,' singular, so one item is enough, like the כוי.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Eliezer holds:
the written tradition is authoritative,
and "mitzvat" (singular) is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר לו רבי אליעזר סבר יש אם למסורת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying principle: the challenging source follows a different reading rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's ruling on the כוי seemed to disprove the need for two items.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר follows the singular spelling, while רב follows the plural reading. Their rulings differ for that reason.

steps.title: A new challenge from a child of doubtful father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a child who may be from the first husband or the second. The man must divorce her, and the child is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא challenged רב: If it is unclear whether the child is a nine-month baby of the first husband or a seven-month baby of the second, he must divorce her, and the child is of fit lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new challenge to רב by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the challenge; its point against רב will become clear as the ברייתא continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a יבום: the יבם married his dead brother's wife, and she gave birth seven months later. If it is a nine-month baby from the first husband, the brother left a child, so the יבום was not allowed and she is forbidden to him as his brother's wife. If it is a seven-month baby from the יבם, the יבום was valid. Because of this doubt he must divorce her. The child is fit either way, since it was not conceived in a forbidden relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt; we don't know which side is true
A baby born after nine months of pregnancy
He must send her out, meaning divorce her
The child is of fit, unflawed lineage

phrases.english: He raised an objection:
If it is uncertain whether the child is nine months old, from the first husband,
or seven months old, from the latter husband –
he must divorce her, and the child is of fit lineage,

steps.triggerLanguage: איתיביה ספק בן תשעה לראשון או בן שבעה לאחרון
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's answer to אביי, the גמרא opens a fresh challenge to רב from a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a doubt about a single item does not require an אשם תלוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא is being set up as a case of doubt about a single situation. The way it challenges רב will appear as the ברייתא continues.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends by requiring an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the ברייתא from step 19 are the actual challenge. Each one is obligated in an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, even though there is only one item of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is obligated to bring an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from step 19. These closing words are the point of the challenge against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible sin is that the יבם was with his brother's wife, if the יבום was not allowed. That is a single doubtful situation, not two items to choose between. Yet the ברייתא still requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי. That contradicts רב, who says a single item of doubt brings no אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.

keyTerms.meaning: A provisional guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned.
Obligated.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new case. It is the ending of the same ברייתא quoted in step 19.

phrases.english: And he is obligated in a provisional guilt offering.
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the ברייתא about the child from the last step. This is the part that bothers רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 19 and states its challenging ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule (step 15) that a single doubtful item does not bring an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי for a single item of doubt, which רב says is exempt.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי even for one item of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר's view, not the view רב follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 18 we learned that רבי אליעזר goes by the singular spelling of the word מִצְוֹת, so for him one item of doubt is enough. A source that matches his opinion does not disprove רב, who follows the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? The גמרא uses this question to assign a source to a specific תנא.
The word in the פסוק. It is spelled like a singular but read as a plural (from step 16).
How a word is written compared with how it is read.

phrases.english: Whose is this?
phrases.notes: He means: which תנא does this ברייתא follow?

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by assigning the ברייתא to רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to prove that everyone requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי for one item of doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי אליעזר holds this, so רב can follow the other view.

steps.title: A challenge from the משנה about blood found on the cloth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in נדה says that if blood is found on her cloth some time after relations, the couple is impure out of doubt and exempt from a חטאת. A teaching added to it says they must bring an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, which again involves only one item of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blood was found on his cloth, they are impure and must bring a קרבן. If it was found on her cloth right away, they are impure and must bring a קרבן. If it was found on her cloth after some time, they are impure out of doubt and exempt from the קרבן. And a teaching added to this says he is obligated in an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב, this time from a משנה in נדה together with a teaching added to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the blood is found later, we don't know if she was a נדה during relations. That is one act and one doubt, not two items. Yet the added teaching requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, which goes against רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure.
An offering. Here it means a חטאת for a definite sin.
Immediately, right away.
After some time has passed.
Impure out of doubt.
A teaching was added about it, explaining or adding to the משנה.

phrases.english: He challenged him:
If blood was found on his cloth –
they are impure, and obligated in an offering.
If on her cloth immediately –
they are impure and obligated in an offering.
If it was found on hers after some time –
they are impure out of doubt
and exempt from the offering,
and it was taught about it:
he is obligated on account of a provisional guilt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב, parallel to step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that one item of doubt brings no אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the 'found after some time' case there is a single doubtful act, yet the teaching requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.

steps.title: This source also follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: the teaching on the נדה משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge exactly like the first: this source follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אליעזר requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי even for one item of doubt, any source that does so can be assigned to him. רב's rule stands for those who disagree with רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The written spelling counts. This is רבי אליעזר's reason (step 18).
A doubt involving a single item.

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources seemed to require an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי for one item of doubt. Both are answered as following רבי אליעזר, so רב's rule survives.

phrases.english: Whose is this?
It is Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 the same way step 21 answered step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The added teaching seemed to be a general rule against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: It reflects only רבי אליעזר's view.

steps.title: רבי חייא quotes רב: two pieces obligate, one piece exempts
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא quotes רב: if one of two pieces (one חלב, one שומן) was eaten and he doesn't know which, he is obligated. If a single piece that may be either was eaten, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said in the name of רב: If two pieces were before him, one of חלב and one of שומן, and he ate one of them and does not know which one he ate, he is obligated. If a single piece might be שומן and might be חלב, and he ate it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's same rule again, this time passed down by רבי חייא instead of רב יהודה (step 15).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The content matches step 15: an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי needs a doubt between two items, not one doubtful item. The גמרא repeats it through a second person who passed it on, which sets up a further discussion of this version.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat, punishable by כרת.
Permitted fat.
A piece of meat or fat.
Which of them.
Exempt.

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same rule as step 15. Only the person passing it on from רב is different (רבי חייא instead of רב יהודה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya said that Rav said:
If two pieces were before him,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חֵלֶב וְאַחַת שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן,
phrases.english: one of forbidden fat and one of permitted fat,
and he ate one of them
and he does not know which of them he ate –
he is obligated.

phrases.aramaic: חֲתִיכָה, סָפֵק שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן סָפֵק שֶׁל חֵלֶב
phrases.english: A single piece, possibly permitted fat, possibly forbidden fat,
and he ate it – he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב's rule, the גמרא brings a second version of the rule, passed down by רבי חייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating one of two pieces (one חלב, one שומן) obligates an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי. Eating a single doubtful piece is exempt.

steps.title: רבי זירא's reason for רב: two pieces can be checked
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains רב's ruling. With two pieces, it is possible to find out which one was forbidden. With one piece, it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: What is רב's reason? He holds that with two pieces, it is possible to clarify their prohibition. With one piece, it is impossible to clarify its prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives his own explanation for רב's ruling from step 24. He explains why two pieces bring an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי but one piece does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there are two pieces, the one left over can be checked, so the doubt can someday be settled. A single piece that is already eaten can never be checked. So רבי זירא holds that an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי applies only to a doubt that could in principle be cleared up.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
He holds (this view)
It is possible to clarify which one is forbidden
A piece (of fat)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a second reason for רב's rule, next to רבא's reason. The rest of this section compares the two reasons.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב?
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: What is Rav's reason?
phrases.notes: This is about רב's ruling in step 24: two pieces make him obligated, one piece makes him exempt.

phrases.english: He holds: two pieces
it is possible to clarify their prohibition,
one piece
it is impossible to clarify its prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason for רב's ruling from step 24. It is a different reason from the one רבא gave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אָשָׁם תָּלוּי requires a doubt that can be clarified. Two pieces can be checked, but a single piece cannot.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between רבא's and רבי זירא's reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether there is any case where רבא's reason and רבי זירא's reason would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between רבא's reason and רבי זירא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a comparison. It asks for a case where the two explanations of רב would give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא explained רב from the plural word ״מִצְווֹת״, which requires two possible items. רבי זירא explained it as needing a doubt that can be checked. In most cases both reasons give the same result, so the גמרא looks for a case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between...?
Reason

phrases.english: What is there between the reason of Rava
phrases.notes: רבא's earlier reason was based on the word ״מִצְווֹת״ being plural, which means there must be two items.

phrases.english: and the reason of Rabbi Zeira?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין טַעְמָא דְּרָבָא לְטַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבי זירא's new reason with רבא's earlier reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two explanations of רב would rule differently.

steps.title: The difference: one olive-size piece and one half-olive piece
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons differ when the pieces are one olive-size and one half olive-size. רבא would exempt him, and רבי זירא would obligate him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a case of an olive-size piece and a half-olive piece. According to רבא, there is no ״מִצְווֹת״, so he is exempt. According to רבי זירא, it is possible to clarify its prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a specific case. There are two pieces, but one of them is only half the size of an olive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A piece smaller than a כְּזַיִת does not count for a חטאת, so for רבא this is really only one item, and the plural ״מִצְווֹת״ is missing. He is exempt. For רבי זירא, the leftover piece can still be checked, so the doubt can be clarified, and he is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
An olive-size piece and a half-olive piece
The plural word in the פסוק, which רבא reads as requiring two items
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's reason: there must be two pieces that count, because of the plural ״מִצְווֹת״. רבי זירא's reason: the doubt must be one that can be checked. They differ with an olive-size piece and a half-olive piece.

phrases.english: The difference between them is an olive-bulk and a half.
phrases.notes: One piece is a full olive-size and the other is only half that size.

phrases.english: According to Rava, there is no "מצוות," so he is exempt,
phrases.notes: A half-olive piece does not count, so there are not really two items here.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Zeira, it is possible to clarify its prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 with a case where the two reasons give different results.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the case of an olive-size piece and a half-olive piece, רבא exempts him because there are not two pieces that count. רבי זירא obligates him because the doubt can be clarified.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה's challenge from the fat of a כוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא. רבי אליעזר requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי for eating the fat of a כוי, even though that doubt can never be clarified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה raised an objection to רבי זירא: רבי אליעזר says that for a כוי, one is obligated in an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי for its fat!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי זירא's reason. He uses a case where an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי is required even though the doubt can never be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוי's status is permanently unclear: no one can ever know whether its fat is forbidden or not. If an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי requires a doubt that can be clarified, as רבי זירא said, then eating its fat should not bring one. Yet רבי אליעזר says it does.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose status is a doubt: maybe a domestic animal, whose fat is forbidden, or maybe a wild animal, whose fat is allowed
Its forbidden fat

steps.confusionAlert: The doubt here is not about which piece he ate. It is about what kind of animal the כוי is, and that question can never be settled.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised an objection to Rabbi Zeira,
Rabbi Eliezer says: A koy,
phrases.notes: A כוי might be a domestic animal or might be a wild animal, so whether its fat is forbidden is a doubt.

phrases.english: one is obligated in a provisional guilt offering for its fat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי זירא gave in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rule that an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי requires a doubt that can be clarified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The status of a כוי can never be clarified, yet רבי אליעזר requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי for its fat.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר does not require a checkable doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that רבי אליעזר holds a different view: he does not require the doubt to be one that can be clarified.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי אליעזר holds that we do not need to be able to clarify its prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. He says the כוי ruling comes from רבי אליעזר, who simply holds a different view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's requirement explains רב, not רבי אליעזר. As we saw in steps 21 and 23, רבי אליעזר requires an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי even for a single doubt. Here רבי זירא states directly that רבי אליעזר also does not need the doubt to be checkable, so the כוי ruling does not challenge רבי זירא's explanation of רב.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not require
Holds (an opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's view stands apart: an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי even for one item, and even when the doubt can never be clarified. רב, as רבי זירא explains him, requires a doubt that can be clarified.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Eliezer holds:
we do not require the ability to clarify its prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a disputing opinion (רבי אליעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that an אָשָׁם תָּלוּי requires a doubt that can be clarified, so the כוי ruling would contradict רבי זירא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רב, as רבי זירא explains him, requires a checkable doubt. רבי אליעזר does not, so the כוי ruling fits his own view.
